name: Used / secondary market: NVIDIA A100 80GB (bare card, ASKING band)
price_basis: USED-market ASKING prices, bare A100 80GB (SXM4-module and SXM4-to-PCIe-converted) cards only, USD, observed 2026-10-03. NOT a sold price. Excludes tax/shipping.
notes: FORM-FACTOR WARNING (added 2026-10-04): this record's accelerator_ids names nvidia-a100-80gb-pcie, but the price_basis explicitly covers 'SXM4-module and SXM4-to-PCIe-converted' cards as well. The secondary market does not cleanly separate form factors, so this band is a MIXED population and must NOT be read as a PCIe-only price. An SXM4 module is useless off its carrier and is not interchangeable with a PCIe card. Treat this as 'A100 80GB, any form factor, secondary market' until a source that separates them exists.

OBSERVATION DATE 2026-10-03. Source sup-price-picclick-ebay-asking. BAND: n=17, quartiles $19,995 (p25) / $21,995 (median) / $29,000 (p75), full range $16,798-$34,999. n=17 gives a usable band. This is the one datacenter line where the ASKING market and the institutional index agree in order of magnitude: Stoa's public A100 80GB index level is $9,490 (sup-price-stoa-index, condition unstated), which sits BELOW the bottom of this asking band. Two readings, both kept: either the institutional mark reflects used/refurb units and this band reflects new-in-box units relisted as used, or one of the two sources is marking something other than a bare card. Unresolved - see status. A100 SXM4 modules specifically cluster tighter and lower ($13,177-$20,290, median ~$13,378) than PCIe parts, the same form-factor artifact as the H100. Excluded from the band: 8-GPU HGX baseboards ($5,999-$54,990), A100X, H800, A800, FOR-PARTS, ECC-error and bulk-lot units.
